title: Example MT exam
description:
BIOL109 MIDTERM EXAM Full Name:
ID Number:
Instructions:
1. Write down your name and ID number on each sheet of the exam.
2. Sign the METU honour code on this page.
3. There should be 9 pages/5 sheets in the exam booklet. Check if your booklet
is complete before you start.
4. The duration of the exam is 90 minutes.
5. You are not allowed to leave during the exam. If you do for any reason, you
will not be able to return to the exam.
6. There are 25 questions. Each question is 4 points.
7. You can only request translation of unknown words (except biological
terms) from the Teaching Assistants.
8. Write down your answers at the provided table on the last page of the exam
booklet. Any answers not written in the table but are marked on the
question will be disregarded.
9. Use capital letters when filling in the answer table. Your choice needs to be
easily legible otherwise it won’t be graded.

1- Which of the following is correct about DNA structure?
1
-- 1 of 7 --
BIOL109 MIDTERM EXAM Full Name:
ID Number:
A. DNA denaturation results in formation of free nucleotides.
B. Nucleotides on the same strand are connected through noncovalent
interactions.
C. If we know the percentages of each nucleotide in a DNA molecule, we can
figure out its sequence.
D. If DNA loses its three-dimensional shape, it may still be able to return to
original structure.
E. Sugar-phosphate backbone of both DNA strands runs in 3’ to 5’ direction.
2- Which of the following is a good example of the dynamic nature of the genetic
material?
A. There are genes that code for proteins that enable organismal/cellular
movement such as flagella.
B. Maternal copy of genes in an organism originates from the haploid genome
of the oocyte.
C. Histone proteins are conserved proteins.
D. If the entire nucleus of an organism X is replaced with the nucleus of another
organism Y (nuclear cloning), the cell will show the phenotype organism Y.
E. Similar genes can adopt new functions in different species.
